Modern villas — Jeddah

Modern villa design in Jeddah

Which room would you like to open to the morning light? Where would you sit in the late afternoon? Those choices and the orientation of your Jeddah plot guide the width of the windows, the position of privacy screens and the shade you need outside the terrace door.

Request a free call WhatsApp

The street facade at Montashiri Villa in Obhur

In the proposed street view above, horizontal slats fill openings in the garden wall. They screen the ground floor from passers-by while palms on the upper terraces remain visible from the street. Behind this facade, the family living room draws daylight from a planted courtyard. On your plot, we check each opening from pavement level and from the windows opposite.

One canopy for the terrace and balcony

In our proposed villa in Khamis Mushait, Asir, a timber-lined canopy extends over the balcony and curved stair. The balcony shelters the seating below. The close view shows the depth of the canopy and the night view traces its edge in light. For a terrace on your Jeddah plot, we start with the hour you’ll use it and check where the shade falls across the seats when the sun is low.

Frequently asked questions about private villa design

How can I shade a west-facing window?

Low afternoon sun can reach the glass beneath a horizontal overhang. We can set the window deeper into the facade or angle an exterior screen, then check how much of the view stays open from inside the room.

What should I bring to the first facade discussion?

Send the plot location, a plan if you have one, and a view from the street. Tell us which room matters most for morning light or afternoon shade. We start with a free call and a free preliminary concept. Once the direction works for you, we agree on scope and fees.

How do you keep privacy with large openings?

By orienting openings toward internal courts and gardens, using architectural screens, and layering levels.
